metadata.name: T1003.001 - Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
metadata.description: Detection and response playbook for LSASS credential dumping techniques used by attackers to extract credentials for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

strategy.detection_approach: Behavioral detection of memory access patterns combined with process monitoring

mission.goal: Detect and respond to LSASS credential dumping attacks within 15 minutes
mission.description: Organizations need visibility into attempts to extract credentials from LSASS process memory. LSASS stores credentials that can be exploited for lateral movement.

layers.description: Monitor for suspicious memory access to LSASS process using Sysmon Event 10
Enrich alerts with process ancestry, file operations, and network connections
Execute automated response actions including isolation and notifications

detection_logic.detection_rule:
title: LSASS Credential Dumping Detection
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 10
    TargetImage: '*lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess:
      - '0x001F0FFF'
      - '0x00100410'
  filter:
    SourceImage:
      - 'C:\\Program Files*'
  condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate memory analysis tools
  - EDR software scans
level: high
blind_spots: Detection may miss dumps using kernel-mode techniques or direct system calls
Encrypted memory regions may bypass heuristics
Timing-based evasion where attacker waits for normal activity patterns

operational_context.goal: Enable SOC teams to detect and respond to LSASS memory dumps within 15 minutes
operational_context.technical_context: LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) stores credentials and authentication tickets in memory. Attackers use tools like Mimikatz, Procdump, or custom tools to dump LSASS memory to extract plaintext credentials and hashes.
false_positives: Legitimate memory analysis tools (WinDbg, IDA Pro)
Windows Defender and other security software scanning LSASS
Performance monitoring tools accessing process memory
operational_context.triage_guidance:
1. Review parent process and user account - service accounts dumping LSASS are highly suspicious
2. Check if parent process is legitimate (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, etc.)
3. Look for process creation events around the same time (Mimikatz process)
4. Correlate with network events to identify command & control connections
operational_context.response_playbook:
1. Isolate host from network (disable network interfaces)
2. Collect memory dump from affected system
3. Terminate the dumping process and parent process
4. Force password reset for all accounts on the host
5. Scan for credentials in logs (Event ID 4688 for process creation)
6. Enable credential guard on domain controllers

testing.test_scenario: Use Mimikatz 'sekurlsa::logonpasswords' or Procdump to dump LSASS memory and verify detection fires
testing.test_expected_output: Alert should fire within 2 seconds with: process name (mimikatz/procdump), user account, source and target process information
testing.test_environment: Windows 10/11 or Server 2019+, domain-joined, with Sysmon enabled

enrichment_steps.name: Get Process Timeline
enrichment_steps.description: Query EDR for all process events for the dumping process and parent

enrichment_steps.name: Check Credential Usage
enrichment_steps.description: Check if dumped credentials were used in network logons

enrichment_steps.name: Get User Risk Profile
enrichment_steps.description: Look up user in identity provider for risk assessment

containment_steps.name: Isolate Host
containment_steps.description: Disconnect host from network to prevent lateral movement

containment_steps.name: Terminate Dumping Process
containment_steps.description: Kill the dumping process and parent processes

containment_steps.name: Force Credential Reset
containment_steps.description: Reset passwords for all user accounts on the host

nodes.name: Windows Sysmon Event Parser
nodes.description: Parse and analyze Sysmon event ID 10 for LSASS access patterns

nodes.name: Access Pattern Analysis
nodes.description: Analyze GrantedAccess values and call stacks to identify suspicious memory access

nodes.name: Enrich with Process Ancestry
nodes.description: Add process tree, command line arguments, loaded DLLs, and network connections

nodes.name: Execute Containment
nodes.description: Trigger automated network isolation and process termination

nodes.name: Notify SOC & Create Incident
nodes.description: Send notifications to SOC team and create incident in tracking system

audit_trail.data_source_robustness: Sysmon Event 10 is reliable and comprehensive for process access monitoring
audit_trail.data_source_maturity: Mature - available since Windows Vista with Sysmon support
audit_trail.notes: This detection is part of the critical infrastructure monitoring program. Tested in production environment with low false positive rate (<0.1% per day).
audit_trail.validation_status: Validated - Tested against Mimikatz and Procdump in controlled environment
